heading: INT. ROADSIDE WAX MUSEUM - HALL OF PRESIDENTS - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ROADSIDE WAX MUSEUM - HALL OF PRESIDENTS - NIGHT
Dim corridor.
Red velvet ropes.
Wax figures stand on low platforms in dusty suits, their glass eyes catching the flashlight beams.
A faded banner: "ONE DAY ONLY - FOREVER."
HARLAN BOONE (40s, museum owner, ring of keys, bathrobe over pajamas) leads four visitors down the hall, lantern swinging.
Behind him: DOLORES KIM (50s, schoolteacher, tote bag), KIT ABERNATHY (20s, backpacker, headlamp), MASON TREVELYAN (30s, salesman, loosened tie), and YVETTE DUBOIS (30s, nurse, scrubs under a parka).
Right this way, folks. The museum closes at six, but I make exceptions for storms.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Thank you, Mr. Boone. We were nearly in a ditch.
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: Best place to be nearly in a ditch is my front door.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Are these all real people?
units.name: KIT

units.text: Wax, miss. All wax.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: They look awfully real.
units.name: MASON

units.text: That's the craft.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: Yvette stops at a figure of Abraham Lincoln.
She reaches out, touches its sleeve, and pulls back.
It's warm.
units.name: YVETTE

units.text: That's the lamp.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: There's no lamp.
units.name: YVETTE

units.text: Harlan keeps walking.
The visitors exchange glances.
Is anyone else getting a weird vibe?
units.name: KIT

units.text: ^Is that wax supposed to be breathing?
units.name: DOLORES

units.text: ^Is that wax supposed to be breathing?
units.name: MASON

units.text: Dolores and Mason speak at once, then look at each other in alarm.
All four turn toward the Lincoln figure.
Its head swivels slowly toward them.
Oh no.
units.name: YVETTE

units.text: Harlan stops at the end of the hall.
Turns.
His smile has changed.
It is wider and wrong.
Don't be rude, folks. They've been waiting a very long time for company.
units.name: HARLAN

units.text: All along the hall, the wax figures stir.
A hand lifts.
A jaw clicks.
A glass eye rolls forward.
